column2: On the authority of Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī al-Badrī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Among the words that people have received from the earliest prophethood is: If you feel no shame, then do as you wish.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.

The hadith shows that modesty (ḥayāʾ) is praiseworthy, and that as it is in this Sharīʿah, so it was in the earlier laws; it is one of the noble character traits that the prophethoods passed down until it reached this nation.

The command in it expresses permission and request when what one would be ashamed of is not forbidden in the Sharīʿah; if it is forbidden, then it is a threat, or [it means] that such things come only from someone whose modesty has gone or diminished.

Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (1/497): “His ﷺ words, ‘Among the words that people have received from the earliest prophethood’, indicate that this is transmitted from the earlier prophets,

and that people circulated it among themselves and inherited it from them generation after generation. This shows that the earlier prophethood brought these words, and that they became widely known among people until they reached the first of this nation.”
He went on to say: “His words, ‘If you feel no shame, then do as you wish’, have two interpretations.

The first is that it does not mean a command to do whatever one wishes; rather, it means censure and prohibition of it. Those who hold this view take one of two approaches. The first is that it is a command meaning threat and warning; the meaning is:

if you have no shame, then do what you wish, for Allah will recompense you for it, like His words, ‘Do whatever you wish; indeed, He sees what you do’ [Fuṣṣilat 41:40], and His words, ‘So worship whatever you wish besides Him’ [al-Zumar 39:15]… This is the view chosen by a group, among them Abū al-ʿAbbās Thaʿlab.

The second approach is that it is a command whose meaning is a statement of fact; the meaning is that whoever has no shame does whatever he wishes, for what prevents one from doing shameful things is modesty,
so whoever has no modesty plunges into every indecency and evil, and into whatever someone with modesty would refrain from. This is like his ﷺ words:

‘Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire’, whose wording is that of a command but whose meaning is a statement, namely that whoever lies about him takes his seat in the Fire.

This is the view chosen by Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām (may Allah have mercy on him), Ibn Qutaybah, Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Marwazī and others; and Abū Dāwūd reported from Imam Aḥmad what indicates a view like this…

The second interpretation of his words, ‘If you feel no shame, then do as you wish’, is that it is a command to do as one wishes, according to the apparent meaning of its words. The meaning is: if what you want to do is something one need not be ashamed of doing before Allah or before people,

because it is an act of obedience or part of fine character and good manners, then do of it as you wish. This is the view of a group of imams, among them Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī al-Shāfiʿī, and something similar is reported from Imam Aḥmad.”

He also said (1/501–502): “Know that modesty is of two kinds. The first is that which is an innate trait and disposition, not acquired; it is among the finest character traits that Allah grants a servant and with which He creates him. That is why he ﷺ said: ‘Modesty brings nothing but good’,
for it restrains one from committing shameful deeds and base character, and urges one to practise noble and lofty character. In this respect it is one of the qualities of faith…

The second is that which is acquired through knowing Allah, His greatness and His nearness to His servants, His watching over them and His knowledge of the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. This is among the highest qualities of faith; indeed, it is among the highest degrees of excellence…

Modesty before Allah may also arise from contemplating His blessings and seeing one's shortcomings in giving thanks for them. If the servant is stripped of both acquired and innate modesty, nothing remains to prevent him from committing shameful deeds and base character, and he becomes as though he had no faith.”
The trait of modesty is one of the noble character traits transmitted from the earlier prophethoods.
Encouragement to modesty and a recognition of its virtue.
Losing modesty makes its owner fall into every evil.
